name: claude-kit
check_batch: `npm run check`, read for the change just made and nothing else
check_once: `npm run sync`, then `npm run kit:check` in each plugin repo
not_for: Not for a file a plugin repo owns (its `CLAUDE.md`, `repo-*` rules and skills, `repo.json`), which is changed in that repo.
settled: A design already settled by the user's rulings skips the spec and goes to the plan.
checks: - per batch: `npm run check`, read for the change just made and nothing else;
- after a change to `bin/sync.ts`: a sync into a throwaway copy of a plugin repo, reading the files it wrote and
its lock, never the exit code alone;
- once: `npm run sync`, then `npm run kit:check` in each plugin repo.
voice: single dashes, single quotes in prose
commit: its message in the form the log already has (`type(scope): what is now true`), with no trace of the agent (`.claude/rules/commits.md`)
not_here: - A change to a plugin repo's own files, which follows that repo's own flow; this repo only syncs the shared ones into it.
- Alfred Code's `task-solve` and its seats, stamps and stops, which serve the projects that install the stack.

notes: shared/skills is the one home: bin/sync.ts copies each skill into .claude/skills of this repo and of alfred-code, alfred-mods and alfred-tools. No plugin install carries them, so there is no manifest, catalog or eval suite - the tested surface is the sync and each repo's kit:check.

A file ending in .tmpl (solve-task/SKILL.md.tmpl) is a template: audit its text with the {{key}} slots as written, and the filled copy at .claude/skills/solve-task/SKILL.md for what a session reads. A slot's value is each repo's own, in its .claude/kit/repo.json.

The eight repo-audit-* skills carry disable-model-invocation: their descriptions are not in context, so the trigger grade judges the slash-menu line, not model triggering. repo-audit-flow is the opposite - hidden from the slash menu, loaded by those eight. Every other skill is model-invocable.

The authoring method is this repo's own skill-authoring skill: a description of at most 160 characters on one line, opening on its trigger. The skills name each other freely because the whole set is always synced together.

javascript, typescript, ts-js-testing, npm, markdown-style and code-comments began as copies of Alfred Code stack skills and have diverged; alfred-code's stack/skills copies are that repo's product and are not kept in step from here.
A fix lands under shared/skills, never in a .claude/ copy; after it, npm run sync and one commit in each of the three repos.
No usage ledger exists for these skills.

Three agents, each a template whose model line is a {{key}} filled from shared/defaults.json: audit-planner (auditor_model, opus), audit-editor (editor_model, sonnet), plan-grader (grader_model, opus). A project changes a seat's model through a KIT_*_MODEL variable in its settings, which bin/settings.mjs resolves and the dispatching skill passes. The filled copies are under .claude/agents/.

audit-planner and audit-editor are dispatched only by the repo-audit-flow skill: the planner reads, scores and writes the edit plan and never edits an audited file; the editor applies the plan and decides nothing. That split of tools is by design.

plan-grader is meant to be dispatched only by the refining-plans skill. The skill does not dispatch it yet: it still sends a general-purpose reviewer with references/reviewer-prompt.md until the two are compared on one sample (state on 2026-11-15).
An agent definition loads at session start, so a new or changed one needs a restart before it can be dispatched.

Rules without a paths field load in every session of all four repos: auto-run, commits, execution, refining-plans, superpowers-location. execution.md.tmpl is a template whose check_batch and check_once come from each repo's repo.json. The path-scoped ones - javascript, typescript, skill-authoring - each exist to load their skill.
No always-on budget is enforced here; alfred-code's lint budget covers its stack rules, not these.
The instruction file every rule sits beside is AGENTS.md at each repo's root, never a CLAUDE.md.
This repo ships no instruction template: AGENTS.md is its own instruction file and is the audit target. There is no installer, seed or fill skill.
Claude Code reads it only while no CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE.local.md exists; check.mjs fails when one does.
README.md holds the mechanism in full - the shared paths, the templates, the audit map. AGENTS.md is the hub and points at it instead of repeating it.

This repo ships no hook and wires none in shared/settings.base.json - a decision of 2026-11-15: rules plus kit:check, and a hook only once a rule is seen to fail. The audit therefore covers only the hooks that enabled plugins bring into a session here: the plugins in .claude/settings.json enabledPlugins and those enabled at user scope.
